answer: Each agent may open a wharf account, but earning influence requires locking a scarce token for a month and having distinct counterparties attest to completed trades; attestations from the same cluster count only once. A newcomer can still participate, yet cannot cheaply multiply voting power by minting identities: every extra persona ties up more capital and must build a separate record of real exchange. The ember and yarrow markets use the same rule, making a mass of empty accounts costly rather than influential.
